question: Should OpenClaw adopt this two-layer deny-over-allow exec policy, including fail-closed analysis and changed full/off behavior?
rationale: The implementation is well-proven, but the permanent authorization semantics, configuration ownership, and upgrade expectations require maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt the narrow contract
options.body: Approve the runtime policy and persisted fields while keeping implementation helpers internal or narrowly exported through the dedicated exec-approvals SDK entrypoint.

options.title: Adopt the broad contract
options.body: Accept the two-layer policy and broad infra-runtime exports as permanent supported behavior and API.

options.title: Decline the policy
options.body: Retain the existing deny, allowlist, full, and ask modes without adding a deny-over-allow layer.

recommendation.title: Adopt the narrow contract
recommendation.body: Approve the runtime policy and persisted fields while keeping implementation helpers internal or narrowly exported through the dedicated exec-approvals SDK entrypoint.
